tee_miner: never write the request to the miner log

The serve-error path printed `{e!r}`. When a request holds a lone surrogate
(half an emoji from a buggy client), httpx's strict UTF-8 encode raises a
UnicodeEncodeError whose repr carries the WHOLE JSON body, so tens of KB of
buyer messages landed in miner.log on every box running this miner. Seen on
operator B300s and on our own k5 workers; that breaks zero data retention
whatever hardware the box runs on.

- `_log_safe_error`: the log line keeps the error type, status and the head of
  the message, never the request (and drops an engine validation error's
  echoed `"input"`).
- `_json_body`: engine request bodies are encoded by us; lone surrogates become
  U+FFFD, so the request no longer fails (the engine's tokenizer rejects them
  too).

* fix(sqlite): hold each store's database open between calls

session() closes every per-call connection, so each store call closed the
database's last connection: SQLite checkpointed the WAL and deleted the -wal
and -shm files, and the next call recreated them. On EFS each of those steps

lifetime, released by close() or when the store is collected, so per-call
closes are never the last. Per read call this cuts lock calls from 26 to 4

Release 478

Zero only clear prism deficits and draw close speed duels

The bottom of a cohort's performance scale is the lowest total only when it is at least three standard deviations of duel luck below even, measured from the squared duel deltas behind that total; otherwise the bottom sits at that threshold, so a few lost duels no longer score 0. Equal-rate speed duels draw when the slower duration is at most 5% above the faster.

Use equal prism duel stakes and charge failed recoveries

Both sides of a duel risk the same stake, a failed recovery costs three stakes of its transfer's first wave, a wave where most participants failed settles neutral, and normalization has no floor.
